references.text: Balaam begins his first prophetic oracle with the same expression 'he took up his parable' (וַיִּשָּׂא מְשָׁלוֹ)
Balaam introduces his second prophetic oracle in the same way with 'he took up his parable and said'
Balaam repeats an almost identical introduction to his fourth prophecy, using the same description of himself
Balaam son of Beor is mentioned as a prophet whom the Israelites killed
The expression 'נְאֻם' (oracle/saying) is used in a similar way regarding prophetic speech from the Lord
Isaiah uses a similar prophetic introduction with 'משא' (burden/oracle) for his visions
Balaam son of Beor is mentioned as one who taught Balak to set a trap for the Israelites
Balaam's error is mentioned as a warning against false teachers
Balaam's teaching is mentioned in connection with warnings to the church in Pergamon
